entitySuffixRule: Must contain the words "limited liability company" or "limited company," or the abbreviations "L.L.C.," "LLC," "L.C.," or "LC." The word "limited" may be abbreviated "ltd." and "company" may be abbreviated "co."
distinguishabilityNote: Must be distinguishable from the name of any LLC, limited partnership, or corporation existing under New Mexico law, any foreign LLC or corporation authorized to transact business in New Mexico, and any name reserved under § 53-19-4. There is no consent route: the only way past a conflicting name is to file with the Secretary of State a certified copy of a final court decree establishing the applicant's prior right to use the name in New Mexico.
nameReservationCostBasis: NMSA 1978 § 53-19-63(H) sets the fee at twenty dollars for accepting an application to reserve a name or for filing a notice of transfer of a reservation, and that is the full cost.
notes: New Mexico's LLC name section sets a designator rule and a distinguishability test but lists no banned or regulated words, so restrictedWords is empty; regulated terms such as bank, trust, and insurance are handled by their own licensing statutes rather than § 53-19-3. The only route past a conflicting name is a certified court decree, not a simple consent letter, which makes New Mexico stricter than most states on this point. The reservation runs 120 days from the date the application is filed, with no renewal provision in the statute; it may be transferred to another person, but § 53-19-4(C) says the transfer does not extend the term. Formation is a low $50 (§ 53-19-63(A)) and New Mexico LLCs file no annual report, which pairs with the state's privacy-friendly reputation. NMSA 1978 is published by the New Mexico Compilation Commission on NMOneSource; the Legislature's own site carries no statute text and links there.
